question: What is Inner Monologue in Moshi and why is it used?
answer: Inner Monologue is a method that decomposes speech into a chain of text, semantic and acoustic tokens and predicts this structured sequence in a hierarchical manner, allowing the same utterance to be represented as both text and speech without switching modalities [1]. It is used because integrating acoustic tokens into the generative model enables generating arbitrary voices and conditions rather than a single speaker, and the hierarchical modeling lets Moshi decompose the generation task without increasing the Transformer sequence length, unlike Chain‑of‑Modality [1]. Additionally, Inner Monologue predicts on a per‑frame basis, so each prediction step outputs a speech frame, making Moshi compatible with real‑time generation and enabling streaming TTS and ASR systems when combined with a delay between token types [1]. This method also significantly improves the linguistic quality of generated speech and provides streaming speech recognition and text‑to‑speech capabilities, achieving a theoretical latency of 160 ms and 200 ms in practice for a real‑time full‑duplex spoken large language model [2].
sources: [1] Moshi (arXiv 2410.00037v1), §2 Related Work, p.5 | [2] Moshi (arXiv 2410.00037v1), §Abstract, p.1
key_facts: predicts time-aligned text tokens before (as a prefix to) audio tokens ; improves factuality and linguistic quality of generated speech

question: What is the purpose of the ratio loss in H-Net?
answer:
The ratio loss is introduced to prevent the model from converging to trivial compression behaviors, such as keeping almost all vectors or compressing too aggressively, by guiding the network toward a target compression ratio [1]. It does this by comparing the fraction of vectors actually selected (𝐹) with the average boundary probability (𝐺), which provides continuous feedback even though 𝐹 is not differentiable [1]. When 𝐹 equals 𝐺, the loss reaches its minimum, encouraging the model to match the desired ratio set by the hyperparameter 𝑁 [1]. Combined with the autoregressive prediction loss, the ratio loss preserves content‑adaptive compression, allowing the model to learn which vectors to retain based on semantic importance rather than following predetermined patterns [2].
